task.description: Validate lib/letflow/design/req188-recurring-timers-and-retention.md against REQ-188's acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml REQ-188 entry, reproduced in full below). Confirm: every acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element (see the design's own section 6 acceptance-criteria map, but re-derive the mapping independently rather than trusting that table); no fenced code blocks reproducing real .ex implementation content are present (signatures/type-shapes/tables only); function signatures are fully specified with input/output types and error shapes; cross-module dependencies and DB impact are stated; open questions are listed explicitly rather than silently resolved (design section 7). Also confirm the moduledoc-mandated deferral statements in section 0 actually name decision 0003 Decision C point 2, ISS-0014's adopted option (a) and rejected option (c), and the CHK-12/escalation_timer_duration gap for SCH-04, per AC 8.
acceptance_criteria: a timer with repeat_expression "R/PT1H" that fires creates exactly one NEW pending timer with fire_at equal to the fired timer's fire_at plus one hour, in the same transaction as the firing -- demonstrated by a test that forces the firing transaction to roll back and asserts NEITHER the status change NOR the new timer persisted
a timer with repeat_expression "R3/PT1H" stops re-arming after its third firing: fired_count reaches 3 and the fourth poll creates no new timer, asserted by counting timers rows
a recurring timer whose instance is cancelled does not re-arm -- the chain terminates, asserted after a cancellation followed by a poll

a recurring timer whose repeat interval is SHORTER than the poll interval fires at most once per poll cycle rather than catching up multiple occurrences in one tick, asserted by an explicit test with the interval set below the configured poll interval
the retention runner is DISABLED by default: with no configuration set, a full poll cycle invokes Letflow.EventStore.archive/1 zero times, asserted rather than assumed

with the retention runner explicitly enabled in config, a poll cycle invokes archive/1 and rows older than the tenant's configured retention are moved to events_archive -- closing the zero-caller gap, asserted by row counts before and after

the retention runner runs on REQ-186's existing scheduler process rather than adding a second independent periodic process to lib/letflow/application.ex, confirmed by git diff of application.ex showing no new ticker child

the moduledoc states that partition_maintenance.zig and partition_retention.zig are deliberately not ported, naming decision 0003 Decision C's partitioning deferral and ISS-0014's adopted option (a) as the blocker, and that SCH-04 escalation timers are deferred because :HUMAN_TASK has no escalation_timer_duration attribute in Letflow's graph schema
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

checks_performed.rearm_insertion_point: Read the real do_fire/2 (lib/letflow/scheduler.ex L219-243). The design's claimed insertion point for maybe_rearm_timer/3 -- one more `with` step after Engine.advance_after_timer_fired/3, before the {:ok, :fired} return, inside fire_timer/2's single Repo.transaction/1 -- genuinely fits the real function's structure.
checks_performed.fire_at_anchor: Anchoring to the fired timer's own scheduled fire_at (not actual fire time) is the correct drift-avoidance choice and matches AC1's literal wording and SCH-07's stated behavior.
checks_performed.at_most_once_per_cycle: Verified against the real poll_and_fire/1 (L149-170) and Poller.handle_info/2 (poller.ex L51-58): claim_due_timer_ids/2 is called exactly once per poll_and_fire invocation, up front, producing a fixed list before any re-armed row can exist. poll_and_fire/1 itself is called once per tenant schema per tick, not per-timer. The design's structural claim holds against the real execution order.
checks_performed.repeat_total_termination: REQ-186's real CHECK constraint (priv/repo/migrations/20260829020001_create_timers.exs L111-118: fired_count >= 0, repeat_total >= 1 when non-null, fired_count <= repeat_total) matches the design's comparison and worked R3/PT1H trace exactly.
checks_performed.poller_state_widening: Grepped test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs and scheduler_test.exs -- no test pattern-matches the Poller's state shape, so widening %{} to %{last_retention_run_at: ...} is compatible. retention_enabled?() genuinely defaults false via the same scheduler_config()[:key] || @default pattern the four existing accessors use.
checks_performed.iss_0014_citation: Read docs/issues/ISS-0014.yaml directly. Its resolution text matches the design's section 0 citation verbatim in substance (adopted (a), rejected (c) 'because it would force partitioning early, contradicting 0003 Decision C's deliberate deferral, and would need REVIEWER sign-off / a new decision record') -- not strengthened or altered.
checks_performed.archive_zero_callers: Grepped lib/ for 'EventStore.archive(' and 'def archive' -- only the definition itself, an unrelated Letflow.Definitions.archive/2, and moduledoc/comment references exist. Zero real call sites confirmed.
checks_performed.chk12_escalation_gap: Read lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex directly -- CHK-12/check_timer_duration/1 (L738) filters :TIMER nodes only; no escalation_timer_duration reference exists anywhere in the file. Claim verified.
checks_performed.no_implementation_code_check: FAILED. Grepped fenced code blocks in the design (10 blocks). Two of them (section 2.3 lines 230-236: a complete two-clause implementation of retention_due?/1 with a real function body; section 2.4 lines 256-264: the literal if/do/else body being added to Poller.handle_info/2, including the real Enum.each call and state-update expression) reproduce real, near-verbatim .ex implementation, not signatures or type shapes. This violates the design-only rule (task acceptance criterion 8 / this project's mechanical no-exceptions rule already hit twice on a different requirement per docs/anti-patterns.md, commits 3680243 and 290c6b2).

result.verdict_statement: FAIL. All ten acceptance criteria map to concrete design elements, and every specific engineering claim checked against real source (re-arm insertion point, fire_at anchoring, at-most-once-per-cycle structural reasoning, CHECK-constraint alignment, Poller state-widening compatibility, ISS-0014/CHK-12 citations, archive/1 zero-callers) holds up under independent verification. The design fails solely on the mechanical no-implementation-code rule: two fenced blocks (retention_due?/1's full body in section 2.3, and Poller.handle_info/2's new if/else body in section 2.4) reproduce real .ex logic rather than signatures. Full findings in the report file. Routed back to CODE-DESIGNER for a narrowly-scoped fix (replace both blocks with prose + bare @spec, matching how the rest of the document already does this).
